lines: # RecipeBox
A small recipe app: keep recipes, scale them by servings, plan the week, shop from the list.
This repository is a **demo**. Its issues, milestones and labels are sample data, seeded once so
that a tool reading a real repository -- its issues, its board, its design notes -- has something to read.
Nothing here is real work, and none of it belongs to anybody.
- `design/` holds the notes a decision came from; `spec/` holds what was decided.
- `docs/` is how to run it.
description: How scaling should treat a pinch, an egg and a third of a cup.
# Scale a recipe by servings
> GitHub: https://github.com/johnfrog76/recipe-box-demo/issues/6
The conversation behind the spec. A recipe for four, cooked for six: every quantity times 1.5.
## What we talked about
- **Countable things round.** One and a half eggs is two eggs, and the step says so.
- **Pinches do not scale.** A pinch of salt for six is still a pinch.
- **Fractions stay fractions.** A third of a cup times 1.5 is half a cup, never 0.5.
## What we left out
Scaling cooking times. A bigger pot is not a longer bake in any rule we could write down.
description: The contract for scaling a recipe by servings.
# Spec: scale a recipe by servings
> GitHub: https://github.com/johnfrog76/recipe-box-demo/issues/6
| Decision | Rule |
| D-1 | A recipe has a base serving count; scaling multiplies every quantity by target / base |
| D-2 | A countable unit (egg, clove) rounds up to a whole number |
| D-3 | A quantity marked `to taste` or `pinch` does not scale |
| D-4 | Quantities are rationals end to end; the display picks the nearest kitchen fraction |
## Acceptance
- 4 to 6 servings: 1/3 cup becomes 1/2 cup, 1 egg becomes 2 eggs, a pinch stays a pinch.
# Running RecipeBox locally
There is no app here yet -- this repository is sample data, a demo that stands on its own.
If there were, this is where `npm install` and `npm run dev` would be explained.

milestones.title: v0.1 -- Cook from it
milestones.description: One recipe on one page, quantities that survive a save, and a way in from the web.

issues.title: Show a recipe's ingredients and steps on one page
body: A recipe opens as two tabs, ingredients and method, and cooking from it means flipping between them with floury hands.
One page: ingredients down the side, steps down the middle.

issues.title: Quantities lose precision on save
body: A third of a cup comes back as 0.33, and three of them no longer make one.
Store quantities as rationals, not floats, and migrate the existing rows.

issues.title: Import a recipe from a URL
body: Every recipe is typed in by hand.
Paste a link; read the page's recipe markup; land on the edit form with everything filled in.

issues.title: Paginate the recipe list
body: The list renders every recipe at once and the page stalls past a few hundred.
Twenty-five a page, with the page in the address so Back works.

issues.title: Search returns duplicates when tags overlap
body: Searching by tag joins recipes to tags and returns one row per match, so a recipe carrying two of the searched tags comes back twice. The count in the header is wrong for the same reason.

issues.title: Scale a recipe by servings
body: A recipe for four, cooked for six, means arithmetic at the stove.
A servings control on the recipe page. The rules are in `spec/scale-a-recipe-by-servings.spec.md`; the conversation behind them is `design/scale-a-recipe-by-servings.md`.

issues.title: Extract unit conversion into a pure module
body: Conversion is copied into three components, and two of them disagree about how many grams are in a cup of flour.
One module, no UI imports, and the three call sites use it.

issues.title: A week planner: drag recipes onto days
body: There is no way to say what is for dinner on Thursday.
Seven columns, drag a recipe onto one, and the shopping list follows.

issues.title: The shopping list double-counts an ingredient used twice
body: Two recipes on the plan that both use onions put onions on the list twice, as two lines.
Merge lines by ingredient and unit; convert where the units differ.

issues.title: Share a recipe as a read-only link
body: Sending a recipe to someone means a screenshot.
A link that opens the recipe without an account. Who can revoke it, and how, is the open question.

issues.title: The print view drops the last step
body: Printing a recipe whose method runs onto a second page leaves the final step off.
Let the method break across pages.

issues.title: Say how to run the app locally
body: Write it once there is an app to run.
